propositions: A configured `provider="bedrock"` is silently discarded when a model id contains a colon in its version suffix (e.g., `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`), because `_resolve_target` incorrectly treats any colon as a provider separator.

The parsing logic wrongly infers a provider name from a model id fragment when the id contains a colon, treating the dotted prefix as a provider instead of part of the model name (e.g., `infer_provider("us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0")` returns `"us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1"` instead of `None`).
Two independent colon-based tests (`_resolve_target` and `infer_provider`) implement the same decision inconsistently, allowing the same defect to be reached by different inputs.
An explicitly configured provider must be checked FIRST before scanning the model string, so no punctuation in a model id can override or silence an explicit instruction.
A configured provider that conflicts with an inline qualifier (e.g., `provider="bedrock"` with model string `openai:gpt-4o`) is silently dropped instead of raising a conflict error.
Canonical Bedrock model ids in versioned form (`...-v1:0`) are broken and only unversioned aliases work, hiding the bug during typical use.
